name: Random Combinations and Permutations
miniText: How do ordering and repeated symbols change the probability of a match? NetLogo Random Combinations and Permutations lets a user select a target configuration, then generates guesses and separately counts exact ordered matches and matches after disregarding order. Durrett [1] supplies finite probability spaces, Jaynes [2] grounds the explicit assignment of probabilities, and Stanley [3] develops enumerative combinatorics, directly grounding the multiplicities created when order is disregarded. The model's own terminology should therefore be interpreted from its comparison rules rather than assumed to match every textbook convention. The number of positions, available symbols, and repeated target symbols determine multiplicities and waiting times. Random search assumes the configured generator, not intelligent inference. Finite success counts fluctuate, and treating all unordered outcomes as equally likely can misrepresent the experiment.
